name: pyBKT
summary: A Python library of Bayesian Knowledge Tracing models that estimate a student's mastery of each skill from their sequence of right and wrong answers.
made_by: Computational Approaches to Human Learning Research Lab, UC Berkeley
cite: Badrinath, A., Wang, F., & Pardos, Z. A. (2021). pyBKT: An Accessible Python Library of Bayesian Knowledge Tracing Models. EDM 2021, 468-474.

fits.how: Computes mastery from learning events out of process (it is Python), beside the harness's own mastery streak, from a template the harness writes.

connect.note: Writes a measure from a template: fit Bayesian Knowledge Tracing on a class's records with pyBKT (which needs Python 3.12 and older packages), then viable-harness measure record.json --component manifest.json gives mastery per skill, beside the harness's own streak. It needs many attempts per skill. Not compared with the streak on real learners.
